chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Maythamī, from Abān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Ten men killed a man. He said: “If his heirs wish, they may kill them all together and pay nine blood-monies; and if they wish, they may choose one man and kill him, and the remaining nine shall pay to the family of the last slain man one-tenth of the blood-money, each man among them.” He said: “Then indeed the wālī undertakes their discipline and imprisonment.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: the heirs or legal guardians of the slain person who hold the right of retaliation
key_terms.الْوَالِيَ: the governing authority responsible for enforcement and discipline
key_terms.دِيَاتٍ: blood-monies owed as financial compensation in a homicide case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when ten people jointly kill one person according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling for a case in which ten men jointly kill one man. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explains the options available to the victim’s heirs in retaliation and the financial liability that follows, and he also states that the wālī is responsible for disciplining and imprisoning the offenders.
